message.reasoning_content:
Now I'm in the improvement phase. I need to decide on improvement: change one or both tip-speed weights.

Key facts: terminal_tip_speed_weight = 0.0, holding_tip_speed_weight = 0.0, tip_speed_scale_m_s = 0.02, settling speed limit 0.02 m/s, holding speed 0.635–1.581 m/s, terminal speed 0.635 m/s. Reach passed. Holding position/speed failed. Computation: mean update 17.26 s vs 0.01 s period, 35/35 deadline misses.

The accepted diagnosis identified zero terminal/holding tip-speed penalty as a "possible" candidate. My job: adopt a bounded experiment with nonempty effective delta.

Disposition: adopt, changing terminal_tip_speed_weight (and possibly holding_tip_speed_weight) to positive values. Since the improvement budget allows local_comparison optional (2 solves, 300 s) with a saved baseline update with effective horizon 0.01 s (that's update id... effective horizon in control intervals — effective_horizon must be 0.01 s? Hmm, "effective plan horizon must be 0.01 s" means horizon = 1 control interval = 0.01 s. Updates with effective_horizon 2 and 4... hmm, we don't have horizon = 1 in the displayed set. Displayed effective horizons: 10, 7, 6, 4, 2. Hmm, but control period 0.01 s → horizon 1 interval = 0.01 s. We have no update with effective_horizon = 1 in the displayed facts. Actually "effective plan horizon must be 0.01 s" — if horizon is in control intervals, 1 interval = 0.01 s. Updates 7 and... we have effective_horizon values 10 at 17, 7 at 28, 6 at 29, 4 at 31, 2 at 33. Hmm, that's odd — earlier list says 10 at update 17, 7 at 28, 6 at 29, 4 at 31, 2 at 33. The handles show updates.4.effective_horizon = 7 and 10 (different artifacts, different executions?), updates.7 = 2, updates.6 = 4, updates.0 = 6.

Hmm, no update with horizon 1. Careful: maybe the requirement "effective plan horizon must be 0.01 s" refers to the horizon in seconds — with control_period_s 0.01 and horizon in control intervals = 1. We don't have evidence of such a saved update. Actually the granted capability says "compare baseline against one selected changed positive weight at a legal saved state... effective plan horizon must be 0.01 s."

Hmm. I could omit local_comparison entirely — it's optional and "omit if unnecessary". Given uncertainty about a legal saved update (no update with horizon of 1 interval observed in displayed evidence; and my read budget is 0 evidence turns — phase_tools include evidence.read but evidence_turn_limit is 0... "evidence_turn_limit":0. So I cannot read evidence. So I cannot verify a legal saved update.

So I should make the decision with the tool call design_decide_improvement, without local_comparison (omit since I can't verify a legal saved update and the grant says omit if unnecessary). Actually should I include it? Risk: choosing an update_id that isn't legal (effective horizon must be 0.01 s). Displayed evidence shows no update with effective horizon 0.01 s. Hmm, but "effective plan horizon" might be in seconds: horizon 10 intervals × 0.01 = 0.1 s. Actually the field unit is "control intervals". So 0.01 s = 1 interval. Not observed → omit local_comparison. Also, screening unavailable/inconclusive does not prohibit the complete experiment.

Now the actual change values. I need to pick weights. Consider the cost: terminal weight on squared world tip speed / tip_speed_scale_m_s (0.02 m/s). Terminal speed 0.635 m/s → normalized squared = (0.635/0.02)^2 = 31.75 → × weight. Holding weight is per-second squared spatial speed weight on nodes at/after settling window start.

The existing terminal_weight is 5.0, terminal_velocity_weight 0.0001, velocity_weight 0.0001, tracking_weight 1.0, tip_speed_scale 0.02. The speeds are ~30× the scale, so squared ~1000× — a weight of even 0.001 gives large cost. Choosing unit-scale weights up to 1.0. Hmm, but I cannot compute the objective; raw magnitudes aren't comparable.

A reasonable, defensible choice: moderate positive values, e.g., terminal_tip_speed_weight = 0.01 and holding_tip_speed_weight = 0.01? Or since holding window is where the failure is (holding speed 0.635–1.581 m/s), the holding weight matters more. But the holding term is "per-second squared spatial speed weight on nodes at/after the configured task settling-window start" — the settling window is 0.05 s = last 5 control intervals of a 10-interval horizon? Hmm, horizon 10 intervals = 0.1 s total; the settling window 0.05 s covers nodes at/after 0.05 s into the plan, i.e., last 5 nodes. So holding nodes exist in the plan only if the horizon extends past 0.05 s (i.e. horizon ≥ 6 intervals). Note earlier diagnosis re: horizon shrinking — but those are different executions/horizon display.

Choose both weights positive? The instruction says "Independently select whether to change one or both weights and their values". The evidence shows failure in both the holding window (position and speed) and terminal speed. The terminal term applies only at the final node; holding applies on the window nodes. Since the observed failure is the entire holding window speed (0.635 to 1.581 m/s, all six samples), the holding tip-speed weight is most directly relevant; terminal tip-speed weight addresses final-node speed.

I'll adopt both with modest positive values, e.g., terminal_tip_speed_weight = 0.01, holding_tip_speed_weight = 0.01. Hmm — is there a risk of "developer-prescribed value"? No prescription given. Need new positive selections ≥ 0.0001 and an effective delta from 0.0. Good.

But should I be more conservative and change just one? The capability says "At most one model-selected changed candidate" for the complete execution — meaning at most one changed candidate configuration (which can contain one or both weights). Fine.

Expected measurable effects:
- Reach: expected unchanged/no material change; terminal precision already inside tolerance; added terminal speed penalty could slightly trade position authority, risk of pushing terminal error toward the 0.01 m tolerance. Must state possible adverse effect: terminal reach could degrade as position/velocity terms are relatively down-weighted.
- Holding position: speed penalty should discourage coasting/drift → error band could shrink; but the added weight is a scalarized trade-off and may redirect authority away from tracking, potentially enlarging position error.
- Holding speed: expected reduction from 0.635–1.58 m/s toward the 0.02 m/s band; magnitude unknown, likely not fully attaining the limit in one run.
- Computation: additional quadratic terms with a nonzero weight may add gradient/Hessian work, but the observed 15 s solve times and max_iterations 120 / max_cpu_s 30 s means the budget-limited stops are unlikely to be relieved; expected neutral-to-slightly-worse solve time, more deadline misses — but no causal claim.

Weakening observations: if one-step projected probe shows no change in predicted terminal/holding speed; if the complete run's holding speed stays >> 0.02 m/s while solve time rises; if reach regresses outside 0.01 m; if solver stops earlier (budget_best_feasible) with no speed change.

Also mention the weights feed the cost only via scale tip_speed_scale_m_s = 0.02 and scheduling unchanged.

Should I include local_comparison? Decision: omit. Rationale: no saved baseline update with effective plan horizon 0.01 s is displayed in the retained evidence I may use (displayed effective horizons 2–10 intervals), evidence read allowance for this phase is zero, so a legal saved update cannot be identified; the grant states unavailable/inconclusive screening does not prohibit the complete experiment. So omit local_comparison. That's the cleanest.

Actually, wait — maybe I should include it with some update? The risk of naming an illegal update is a protocol/business failure. Omit. The field is optional ("omit if unnecessary").

Now compose the call: disposition "adopt", changes with both weights, rationale, expected_measurable_effect.

Note: instructions say "Preserve terminal speed cost as a single terminal scaled squared-speed term, and holding speed cost as an integration-step-weighted sum at scheduled holding nodes; scale and scheduling remain unchanged." I should state that in rationale.

Field names in schema: "control/recipe/holding_tip_speed_weight" and "control/recipe/terminal_tip_speed_weight" as properties of changes object.

Let me write the rationale with concrete values and hypotheses, and expected_measurable_effect describing per-quantity expectations.

Values: I'll pick terminal_tip_speed_weight = 0.02 and holding_tip_speed_weight = 0.05? Hmm, arbitrary precision may look like inventing. Better to pick simple documented values with rationale based on normalization: with tip_speed_scale_m_s = 0.02, a speed of 0.635 m/s contributes normalized squared 1008; weight 0.01 → 10 in cost units, comparable to terminal_weight 5.0 scale. That's a reasoned anchor, though it involves derived numbers... "Derived numbers require a retrieved computation result; do not invent a derived numerical fact." Computing (0.635/0.02)^2 = 1008 would be a derived number. I should avoid presenting derived arithmetic. Hmm, the rule is about facts in the report; but safer to avoid explicit derived values and speak qualitatively: "given tip_speed_scale_m_s = 0.02 m/s and observed holding speeds near 0.6–1.6 m/s, even a small positive weight produces a large normalized squared-speed term relative to existing weights."

But citing "0.6–1.6 m/s" comes from retrieved facts (fact-holding-speed handles). But I don't have fact handles bound in this phase's catalog? The catalog has handles, e.g., f6e559a48d2e3 for late_max_speed_m_s, f1f64e7822033 for speed min, f7122606cbc95 for holding_tip_speed_weight, f0248154554ed for terminal_tip_speed_weight, f397d3e1b99f2 holding_speed_passed false, f54ca01aba7ed sampled_settling_passed false, f40b212aa9b06 reach_passed true, f0e42f37e4271 terminal_error_m, fbe6bbadcab5b deadline_misses 35, f12300b55c7c2 mean_update_s.

Hmm — but the tool schema for design_decide_improvement has no fact handles field (no fact_selectors). The instruction says "Select fact_handles for your own concise factual statements" — but this tool doesn't accept fact_selectors. So skip.

Choose values: terminal_tip_speed_weight = 0.01, holding_tip_speed_weight = 0.05.

Hmm, should holding be larger than terminal since the failure window evidence (6 samples, all six failing positions and speeds) is the holding window? Justify: holding term acts over the window's scheduled nodes and is the term whose support matches the failing window; terminal term acts at one node. I'll set holding 0.05 and terminal 0.01. Both ≥ 0.0001 and positive deltas from 0.

Write rationale and expected effect.

Also I must not claim causality. State hypothesis as candidate, not cause.

Also mention possible adverse effects: relative down-weighting of tracking/terminal position → risk of pushing terminal_error_m toward/over 0.01 m; larger cost magnitude could worsen solver conditioning → longer solves/deadline misses; holding-term activation only if plan horizon covers the settling window (horizon must exceed window_s/control_period_s nodes) — hmm, that's derived arithmetic (0.05/0.01 = 5). Avoid; phrase: "the holding term only acts on nodes at/after the configured settling-window start, so plans whose effective horizon is shorter than that window contribute no holding cost." That's a qualitative statement — fine? The horizon must extend past the window start for nodes to exist. That's structural understanding, acceptable, and framed as a caution without numbers.

Observations that would weaken the hypothesis: complete run in which holding/terminal speeds remain far above 0.02 m/s and track the baseline, or local screening showing no change in predicted speeds at the changed weight; a rise in deadline misses/solve times without speed reduction; reach regressing.

Now write the tool call.

function.arguments: {"disposition": "adopt", "changes": {"control/recipe/terminal_tip_speed_weight": 0.01, "control/recipe/holding_tip_speed_weight": 0.05}, "rationale": "Bounded experiment on the accepted diagnosis: the retained baseline (execution cf997605885642759ee33920e2c9e2ef, controller.gvs_nmpc 7.0.0, parameters 1.0.0, numerical_source bundled_guess) records reach_passed = true with terminal_error_m 0.007642608585867386 m inside reach_tolerance_m 0.01 m, but holding_speed_passed = false over the six recorded final-window samples (speed_m_s 0.6351726092425104 to 1.5810152739742807 m/s, terminal_speed_m_s 0.6351726092425104 m/s) and holding_position_passed = false over the same window, against settling_criteria speed_limit_m_s 0.02 m/s and position_limit_m 0.01 m. The recipe records terminal_tip_speed_weight = 0.0 and holding_tip_speed_weight = 0.0 with tip_speed_scale_m_s = 0.02 m/s, i.e. both tip-speed penalties are currently disabled, which is the testable candidate identified in the diagnosis (status \"possible\"; raw weight magnitudes do not establish relative cost-term importance and no causality is claimed). Hypothesis to test: a small positive penalty on squared tip speed will add a cost incentive against residual holding-window motion that the position/velocity terms alone did not remove. I select both weights positive because the failure evidence is split between window motion across the whole window (holding term, whose support is the nodes at/after the settling-window start) and the final-node speed (terminal term, a single scaled squared-speed term); the holding value is set larger (0.05 vs 0.01) because its support covers the failing window rather than one node. Values are deliberately small relative to tip_speed_scale_m_s = 0.02 m/s, so that with observed ~0.6-1.6 m/s speeds the added term is material but not dominant over tracking_weight 1.0 and terminal_weight 5.0. Structure is preserved exactly as instructed: terminal speed cost stays a single terminal scaled squared-speed term, holding speed cost stays an integration-step-weighted sum at the scheduled holding nodes, and both the scaling (tip_speed_scale_m_s) and the node scheduling (settling window_s = 0.05 s) are unchanged. No local_comparison is requested: this phase has no evidence read allowance, displayed per-update effective_horizon values for the retained records are 2, 4, 6, 7 and 10 control intervals, and no saved baseline update whose effective plan horizon is 0.01 s is displayed, so a legal saved state cannot be identified from what I may consult; the grant states unavailable/inconclusive screening does not prohibit the complete experiment, so the single complete changed candidate is requested instead.", "expected_measurable_effect": "Expected recordable effects of the complete experiment versus the baseline record, stated separately and without causal attribution. Terminal reach: expected approximately unchanged; if the added tip-speed cost trades away position authority, terminal_error_m could drift upward toward the recorded 0.01 m reach tolerance, so reach_passed = true should be re-checked as an acceptance guard. Sampled holding position: ambiguous directionally; the same six-sample final-window statistics (error_m range 0.007642608585867386-0.05813810428573256 m in the baseline) may contract if residual motion was driving position wander, or may widen if relative down-weighting of tracking increases drift. Sampled holding speed: this is the primary target - expect holding-window speed_m_s range and terminal_speed_m_s to move below the baseline 0.6351726092425104-1.5810152739742807 m/s band; full attainment of the 0.02 m/s settling speed limit within one complete run is not expected, so a reportable partial reduction is a useful outcome. Computation: expected neutral-to-slightly-worse; adding nonzero quadratic tip-speed terms can add solver work, and with mean_update_s 17.26331904856488 s against control_period_s 0.01 s, deadline_misses 35 of 35 update_count and stopping_counts User_Requested_Stop 34 / Solve_Succeeded 1, the run may still stop on budget rather than tolerance, so no solve-time improvement is predicted. Possible adverse effects to watch: terminal_error_m regressing past reach_tolerance_m; larger cost magnitude worsening solver conditioning, iteration count or deadline misses; and the holding term contributing nothing on plans whose effective horizon does not reach the configured settling-window start, which would leave the enlarged holding cost inert and make a null speed result uninformative. Observations that would weaken the hypothesis: a complete run whose holding-window and terminal speeds stay in the baseline band while deadline misses or solve times rise; a pattern of budget-limited stops (budget_best_feasible-type) with no speed or position change; a terminal reach regression with no speed benefit; or any future local screening at a saved update showing no change in projected terminal/holding speed at the changed weight."}
function.name: design_decide_improvement
